main_body: A small nightstand: a wide tabletop slab that overhangs a narrow body with a drawer and a handle, standing on two legs with a gap between them.
top_band: Light orange-tan top surface at rows 17-18 (L157), stepping to a mid orange at rows 19-20 (L130). Row 21 is a darker front edge (L101) and row 22 is a dark eave shadow (L38).
evidence: The top slab is wider than the body and is about 4 rows of lighter horizontal surface. A distinct darker front-edge row (21) closes it, and a near-black shadow row (22) sits directly under it. Below that, the front face (rows 23-28) is set back and holds an inset drawer with a handle, plus two legs with an open gap between them. This matches the green 'seat: top 5 + legs' and cabinet examples. There is no receding side face. The top is slightly thin, but it is more than a rim and reads as a surface.

style.evidence: The outline is a tinted dark brown (0% neutral edge pixels), which fits the Beodeul standard. The shading is shallow, though. The piece has only 8 distinct colours against 38-40 in the references, and 8 colours per tile against 17-20. The main material ramp is about 4 wood tones, against 5-6 in the references. The tabletop and the drawer are mostly smooth fills with only a faint grain patch on the right of the top, and there are no per-plank highlights or speckle. Next to the stall and the well, it looks thinner and flatter.
